knowledge-base.overview: Fiber v2.50+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for high-performance Go REST APIs. Built on Fasthttp, Fiber provides an Express-like API with zero memory allocation in hot paths. Covers application setup, dependency injection, route grouping, JWT middleware, role-based access, generic body validation, response helpers, custom error handler, and graceful shutdown. Loaded automatically when agents work on Fiber-based .go files.

core-principles.principle: Fiber uses Fasthttp, not net/http. fiber.Ctx is not compatible with net/http interfaces. Use c.Context() to get a context.Context for service calls.
handler -> service -> repository. Handlers are thin: parse, validate, delegate, respond. No business logic in handlers.
Configure a single ErrorHandler on fiber.Config for consistent error responses across the entire application.
Add middleware to the app in order: requestid, logger, recover, cors, helmet, limiter.
Use app.ShutdownWithContext(ctx) with a 30s timeout and close database connections after shutdown.

guardrail.rule: Always configure a custom ErrorHandler on fiber.Config. Never rely on the default HTML error page.
Never store business logic in handlers. Handlers call services only.
Never expose stack traces or internal error details to clients. customErrorHandler returns only safe messages.
Validate all inputs via go-playground/validator. Never process a request body without validation.
Use helmet middleware for security headers in all production deployments.
Use limiter middleware with per-IP key generation to prevent abuse.
Use c.Context() (not c.UserContext) when passing context.Context to services and repositories.
Apply auth middleware at the group level, not per-route. Use RequireRole for fine-grained access.
Use dependency injection throughout. No global state; wire layers in main.go.
Enable Prefork in production for multi-core utilization. Configure read/write/idle timeouts on fiber.Config.

Layer responsibilities: - handler/ HTTP: BodyParser, ValidateBody, call service, respond - service/ Business logic; accepts context.Context only - repository/ Data access; returns domain errors - model/ Domain types and DTOs with validation tags - middleware/ Fiber middleware functions - router/ Route registration with versioning
